answer: An agent economy can require each account seeking rewards to post a bond and forfeit it if audits show several accounts share a controller, funding source, or signing key. Rewards accrue only after a long horizon, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot quickly multiply payouts. The attacker must lock capital into each account and risks losing it; hiding links and maintaining distinct behavior adds cost. A bridge can compare records across domains, while a cedar username proves nothing.
